definition.simple: A contract that gives its buyer a right, but not a duty, to buy or sell something at a set price by or on a set date. The seller takes on the duty.
definition.balanced: The buyer pays a [[option-premium|premium]] for the right. A [[call-option]] is a right to buy; a [[put-option]] is a right to sell, at the [[strike-price]], until or at [[expiry]]. The seller, or [[option-writer|writer]], must deliver, or pay the cash difference, if the buyer [[exercise|exercises]]. Each contract's specification sets the [[underlying]], how many units it covers, the [[exercise-style]] and how it settles.
